To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The ability to utilize iron from the siderophore, ferrichrome, is a variable trait within a population of mesorihzobia and is associated with the presence of genes for the ferrichrome uptake system.

the ability to utilize the ferrichrome siderophore as an iron source in Mesorhuzobium spp. is controlled by three loci that evolved through independent acquisition of genes and deletion of pseudogenes.

the ability to use ferrichrome as the iron source was found as a variable trait in the field population of Mesorhizobia; that genes required for ferricrome utilization are located on three loci and that they were coordinately regulated by iron availability; that the three loci evolved through independent acquisitions and deletions and that the ability to utilize ferichrome was most correlated with the presence fhuA gene.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the evolution of the fhu system, and we propose that this is an example of a three-gene locus evolving through cycles of gene loss and acquisition, and the maintenance of this locus is a result of positive and negative selection pressures.
the evolution of a three-organism symbiotic system.
the microevolution of the fhu gene system in Mesorhiza, a process that has implications for the ecology and evolution of the bacteria in this genus.

the fhu genes have evolved through a complex history that includes multiple independent acquisitions of the fhu2 gene and deletions at the fhu3 and fhu2 loci.
the genetic diversity of fhu genes in a field population was the result of the combined effects of horizontal gene acquisition, gene deletion, and gene regulation.
the fhu system has evolved by gene acquisition and loss, and that the genes are regulated in a coordinated manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the genetic system that allows Mesorhizobia to use ferrichrome as a source of iron has evolved in a manner that is consistent with the theory of the Red Queen.

we found that a mesorhizaobial population is highly variable in their ability to utilize the ferrichrome siderophore and that this variation was correlated with the presence and organization of the fhu gene cluster.
the fhu locus evolved through small-scale acquisition and deletion events and is under the influence of both positive and negative selection pressures.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the genetic architecture of a siderophore utilization system is highly plastic and can evolve through small-scale gene acquisitions and deletions, which may explain the rapid evolution of siderophore utilization systems.
the ability to utilize the iron-siderophore complex ferrichrome is not a single locus trait but a three-loci trait in Mesorhiziobium loti R88B.
